title: The Earthquake That Turned Solid Ground Into Liquid 😱
script: Solid ground can liquefy in seconds — swallowing buildings whole without a single crack first. It's called liquefaction. When the 1964 Alaska earthquake hit at magnitude 9.2, entire neighborhoods in Anchorage didn't crumble — they sank. The soil stopped behaving like solid and started flowing like wet concrete. Streets dropped 10 feet. Houses tilted at 45-degree angles. But here's the terrifying part — this happens beneath ground that looks completely normal from above. No warning. No visible weakness. Send this to anyone who thinks an earthquake only breaks things. Which is why.
search_summary: Soil liquefaction during the 1964 Alaska earthquake caused entire Anchorage neighborhoods to sink as ground turned to liquid.
comment_question: Would you trust solid ground after knowing this? 😨
